text: Introduction to Web Development. The Building Blocks: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Web development consists of three core frontend technologies. HTML provides the structural skeleton of every webpage. CSS styles the appearance, colors, layout, and responsiveness. JavaScript adds interactivity, logic, animations, and dynamic behavior.

Basic Document Structure & DOCTYPE. Standard HTML5 Document Type Declaration. Every modern HTML document begins with <!DOCTYPE html>. DOCTYPE is not a tag; it is an instruction to the web browser. Informs the browser to render the page in modern HTML5 standards mode. Prevents browsers from falling back into legacy quirks mode.

Document Anatomy: <head> & <body>. Separation of Metadata and Rendered Content. <html> is the root element that wraps all content in the document. <head> stores machine-readable metadata not directly visible to users. <body> contains all visual elements: text, images, buttons, and layouts. A valid document must have exactly one head and one body inside html.

Document Metadata: Charset & Title. Essential Elements Inside the <head>. <meta charset="UTF-8"> supports all global characters and emojis. <title> defines the webpage title shown in browser tabs and search results. The title tag is a critical on-page ranking factor for SEO. Always place charset declaration as early as possible inside <head>.

HTML Tags, Elements, and Attributes. Syntax Anatomy of HTML Markup. An element consists of an opening tag, content, and a closing tag. Opening tags can contain key-value attributes like class, id, or href. Self-closing (void) elements like and
do not require closing tags. Attributes always appear inside the opening tag: name="value".

Headings Hierarchy (<h1> to <h6>). Structuring Page Content Logically. Headings range from <h1> (highest importance) down to <h6> (lowest). <h1> represents the main topic of the page; use only one <h1> per page. Never skip heading levels (e.g., do not jump from <h1> directly to <h3>). Screen readers use heading levels to allow users to navigate page sections.

Paragraphs and Text Formatting. Organizing Prose with Semantic Text Elements.

Hyperlinks with the Anchor Tag <a>. Connecting the Web Through Hypertext. Hyperlinks are defined using the <a> (anchor) element. The href attribute specifies the destination URL or page anchor. target="_blank" opens the link in a new browser tab. rel="noopener noreferrer" protects security when opening external links.

Displaying Images with the Tag. Visual Media and Accessibility Attributes. Images are embedded using the self-closing element. The src attribute specifies the image path (relative or absolute URL). The alt attribute provides alternative text when images fail to load. Alt text is legally and ethically required for visually impaired screen readers.

HTML Lists: Ordered and Unordered. Presenting Sequential and Bulleted Information. <ul> defines an unordered bulleted list. <ol> defines an ordered numbered list. <li> defines individual list items inside either list type. Lists are widely used for navigation menus, features, and instructions.

Building a Complete HTML Webpage. Assembling Components into a Working Prototype. Combine doctype, head, body, headings, paragraphs, links, and images. Save the file with the .html extension (e.g., index.html). Open directly in any modern browser by double-clicking or dragging. No server is required to view static HTML on your local computer.

Developer Tools & Code Inspection. Inspecting the DOM in Chrome DevTools. Right-click any webpage element and select 'Inspect' (or press F12). The Elements tab displays the live Document Object Model (DOM) tree. You can test live HTML edits and observe instant updates in the browser. The Console tab alerts you to broken image paths and network errors.

Introduction to HTML5 Multimedia. Native Audio and Video Without External Plugins. Prior to HTML5, media playback required third-party plugins like Flash. HTML5 introduced native <video> and <audio> elements directly in the browser. Provides high performance, hardware acceleration, and battery efficiency. Allows full programmatic control via JavaScript APIs and CSS styling.

The HTML <video> Element. Syntax and Basic Configuration. The <video> tag wraps video content and playback configuration. Specify dimensions using width and height attributes in pixels. Always define dimensions to prevent Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). Include fallback text inside the tag for ancient browsers lacking support.

The 'controls' Attribute. Providing User Playback Control. The controls attribute is a boolean attribute. Displays native browser playback buttons: play/pause, seek bar, and volume. Allows users to enter fullscreen mode and adjust playback speed. Never hide playback controls unless providing a custom JavaScript UI.

Multiple Video Sources with <source>. Cross-Browser Codec and Format Compatibility. Different browsers historically supported different video codecs. Use multiple <source> tags inside <video> for format fallbacks. List modern WebM first for smaller file size, followed by standard MP4. The type attribute specifies MIME type and helps browsers choose instantly.

Autoplay, Muted, and Loop Attributes. Controlling Automatic Playback Behavior. autoplay: Starts video playback immediately as soon as page loads. muted: Sets audio volume to zero (silence) by default. loop: Automatically restarts the video from the beginning upon completion. Commonly used together for hero video backgrounds on landing pages.

Modern Browser Autoplay Restrictions. Protecting Users from Unwanted Audio Disruptions. Modern browsers block unmuted autoplay to prevent intrusive noise. Autoplay will strictly fail unless the video element is also marked 'muted'. Requires user interaction (click/tap) before audio playback is permitted. Always combine autoplay with muted: <video autoplay muted>.

Custom Video Posters with 'poster'. Displaying Preview Images Prior to Playback. The poster attribute specifies an image displayed before video plays. Serves as the video thumbnail while downloading the first media frame. Improves perceived loading speed and user experience significantly. Use crisp, lightweight JPEG or WebP images matching video aspect ratio.

The HTML <audio> Element. Embedding Audio Clips, Music, and Podcasts. The <audio> element is specifically designed for sound without video frames. Supports controls, autoplay, muted, and loop attributes. Universal formats: MP3 (standard), AAC, and modern Ogg Vorbis. Renders compact audio player widgets in all modern browsers.

Supported Media Formats & Codecs. Choosing the Right Compression for the Web. MP4 (H.264 / AAC): The universal standard supported by 99.9% of devices. WebM (VP9 / Opus): Highly compressed, open-source format with smaller size. Ogg / Theora: Open formats primarily used in open-source ecosystems. Recommendation: Provide WebM for fast desktop loading and MP4 for fallback.

Embedding External Content with <iframe>. Integrating YouTube, Google Maps, and Third-Party Media. The <iframe> (inline frame) embeds another HTML document inside current page. Commonly used to embed YouTube videos, Spotify players, and maps. Use allowfullscreen to permit fullscreen playback inside the frame. loading="lazy" defers loading off-screen iframes until user scrolls.

Responsive Media Layouts with CSS. Making Videos and Iframes Mobile-Friendly. Hardcoded pixel widths cause horizontal overflow on mobile screens. Use CSS max-width: 100% and height: auto on video tags. For iframes, use CSS aspect-ratio: 16 / 9 for responsive scaling. Ensures fluid viewing across mobile phones, tablets, and desktop displays.

Web Accessibility for Media: The <track> Element. Captions, Subtitles, and Internationalization. Accessibility is a legal and ethical requirement for modern web apps. The <track> element adds subtitles and captions using WebVTT format (.vtt). kind="subtitles" provides translations; kind="captions" includes audio cues. srclang specifies the language code (e.g., 'en', 'hi', 'es').

Common Multimedia Pitfalls to Avoid. Optimizing Performance and User Experience. Pitfall 1: Uploading uncompressed 4K video files directly to web servers. Pitfall 2: Forgetting the muted attribute on autoplaying videos. Pitfall 3: Omitting width and height attributes, triggering layout shifts (CLS). Pitfall 4: Neglecting fallback formats for mobile Safari or older clients.

Lecture 2 Summary & Key Revision. Recap of HTML Multimedia Concepts. HTML5 native <video> and <audio> provide performant media playback. Always offer controls and include multiple <source> tags for fallbacks. Browser policies require muted for autoplay functionality. Embed third-party streams with <iframe> and add captions with <track>.

Introduction to Search Engine Optimization. Making Websites Discoverable on Google. SEO (Search Engine Optimization) is the process of improving organic visibility. Search engine crawlers (Googlebot) read and index HTML structure. Well-structured HTML ranks higher and drives free organic user traffic. On-page technical SEO begins with clean semantic HTML tags and metadata.

The Crucial <title> Element. Your Webpage's Most Critical Meta Tag. The <title> tag appears as the clickable blue headline in search results. Appears in the browser tab and when sharing links on social platforms. Best Practice: Keep titles between 50 and 60 characters for full display. Include the primary keyword near the beginning of the title string.

The <meta name="description"> Tag. The Search Result Snippet Description. Provides a concise summary of page content below the title headline. Influences Click-Through Rate (CTR) directly from the search results page. Best Practice: Keep meta descriptions between 140 and 160 characters. Include a compelling call-to-action (e.g., 'Learn HTML free today').

Responsive Viewport Configuration. Mobile-First Indexing and Viewport Scaling. Google uses mobile-first indexing: mobile pages determine ranking. The viewport meta tag ensures pages scale correctly on mobile devices. width=device-width sets width to match the screen's physical pixels. initial-scale=1.0 sets the initial zoom level when first loaded.

Semantic HTML for Search Engines. Meaningful Elements vs Generic <div> Tags. Semantic elements describe their meaning to both browser and developer. Use <header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <section>, and <footer>. Replaces meaningless generic <div> soup with clear content boundaries. Helps search engines identify primary content from navigation boilerplate.

Image SEO & Alt Text Optimization. Ranking in Google Images and Image Accessibility. Search engines cannot directly 'see' images; they read the alt attribute. Write clear, descriptive alt text explaining image contents accurately. Include relevant keywords naturally without spamming keyword lists. Use modern compressed formats like WebP or AVIF for fast image loading.

Introduction to Core Web Vitals. Google's Official User Experience Ranking Signals. Core Web Vitals are official Google ranking signals measuring page speed. Focuses on three real-world metrics: Loading, Interactivity, and Stability. LCP measures perceived loading speed of the largest visual element. INP measures how quickly the page responds to user clicks and taps. CLS measures visual layout stability and prevents unexpected shifts.

Largest Contentful Paint (LCP). Measuring Loading Performance for Main Content. LCP marks the point when the page's main content has likely loaded. Measures the render time of the largest image or text block in viewport. Target Threshold: Under 2.5 seconds is rated 'Good' by Google. Fixes: Compress hero images, use CDN hosting, and remove render-blocking CSS.

Interaction to Next Paint (INP). Measuring Responsiveness to User Input. INP replaced First Input Delay (FID) as the official responsiveness metric. Measures the latency of all user interactions (clicks, taps, typing). Target Threshold: Under 200 milliseconds is rated 'Good'. Fixes: Break up long JavaScript tasks and avoid blocking the main thread.

Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). Ensuring Visual Stability During Page Load. CLS measures unexpected layout shifts of visible elements as resources load. Prevents frustrating misclicks when buttons move while you tap them. Target Threshold: Score under 0.1 is rated 'Good'. Fixes: Always declare width and height on images, videos, and ads.

Auditing with Google Chrome Lighthouse. Comprehensive Automated Quality Inspection. Lighthouse is an automated auditing tool built into Chrome DevTools. Evaluates Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO scores (0–100). Identifies unoptimized images, unused CSS, and missing meta tags. Provides specific, actionable recommendations for optimization.

Practical Optimization Techniques. High-Impact Performance Improvements. 1. Modern Formats: Convert JPEG/PNG to modern WebP or AVIF formats. 2. Lazy Loading: Add loading="lazy" to off-screen images and iframes. 3. Script Loading: Use defer or async on external script tags. 4. Asset Minification: Minify CSS and JavaScript to reduce byte size.

Common SEO Misconceptions. Separating Outdated Myths from Effective Strategies. Myth 1: 'Keyword stuffing increases rankings' — Google penalizes spam. Myth 2: 'Meta keywords tag matters' — Ignored by Google since 2009. Truth 1: Focus on user search intent, clear answers, and fast page load. Truth 2: High-quality, original educational content always wins over hacks.

Lecture 3 Summary & Course Wrap-up. Recap of SEO, Core Web Vitals & Web Fundamentals. Technical SEO begins with accurate <title>, meta description, and semantics. Core Web Vitals are Google ranking signals: LCP (speed), INP, and CLS. Audit your projects regularly using Chrome Lighthouse. You now understand HTML structure, media embedding, and web optimization!
